explanation:
# alu8 synthesis and pre-layout STA report (Sienna)

Source of every number: `reports/synth_tool.json` (OpenLane 2 run `run_01M44DR7XRWAQ9XY53AG8SRJCM/pnr/runs/it1`, netlist `06-yosys-synthesis/alu8_top.nl.v`). Constraints: `constraints/constraints.sdc` (13.333333 ns clock, 0.25 ns uncertainty, 4.0 ns DEFAULT input/output delays, ideal clock).

## Synthesis
| Item | Value (from tool) |
|---|---|
| Standard cells | 182 |
| Total cell area | 1938.1088 um^2 |
| Cell classes (flop count) | not provided (`cell_classes` is empty) |

The flop count required by REQ-016 (exactly 12) cannot be confirmed from this data; see open issues.

## Pre-layout STA (ideal clock, no wire parasitics from layout)
| Corner | Worst setup slack (ns) | Worst hold slack (ns) |
|---|---|---|
| nom_tt_025C_1v80 | 6.009780843078964 | 0.38126164415818947 |
| nom_ss_100C_1v60 | 2.917003610112311 | 1.0364853713124358 |
| nom_ff_n40C_1v95 | 7.217461055318085 | 0.1389496473876063 |

The tool names `nom_ss_100C_1v60` as the worst corner. All worst slacks reported are positive, so the tool shows no setup or hold violations at these three corners pre-layout (setup WNS and TNS are therefore 0 at each corner). The smallest hold margin is at the fast corner (0.1389 ns), which is the one to watch after clock-tree synthesis adds real skew. This is a pre-layout result only; REQ-014 is judged on the post-route netlist.

## Worst setup paths at nom_ss_100C_1v60 (plain English)
The tool output contains two complete paths and a third that is cut off; I do not have the worst 10.

**Path 1 - slack 2.917004 ns (MET).** Starts at input port `op[0]` (the low opcode bit, launched 4.0 ns after the clock edge by the DEFAULT input delay) and ends at the D pin of flip-flop `_351_` (`sky130_fd_sc_hd__dfxtp_2`). Data arrives at 9.868275 ns; it is required by 12.785278 ns (13.333333 period - 0.25 uncertainty - 0.298055 setup time). The path goes through 12 logic cells (or3b, a21o, and3, a21o, a211o, a41o, a21oi, and2b, a21o, a21o, o31a). What dominates:
- The 4.0 ns external input delay is the largest single part (about 40% of the 9.868 ns arrival).
- The first gate, `_178_` (or3b_2), takes 1.179272 ns. It is driven through its inverted input C_N by `op[0]` (fanout 9) and itself drives 6 loads; it is the slowest cell on the path. It looks like an opcode decode term feeding the arithmetic/result-select logic.
- The rest is a long chain of AND-OR cells (each roughly 0.35 to 0.64 ns), i.e. logic depth, not a single bad cell. Internal logic delay from the input pin to the flop is 9.868275 - 4.111271 = 5.757004 ns.

**Path 2 - slack 2.940914 ns (MET).** Same start (`op[0]`) and the same first six cells (through `_209_`), then branches via `_211_` (and3), two nor2 gates, `_258_` (or3b_2, 0.997334 ns), `_268_` (a32o) and `_316_` (and4b) into flip-flop `_342_`. Arrival 9.848308 ns, required 12.789222 ns. Dominated again by the 4.0 ns input delay plus the two or3b_2 cells (1.179272 ns and 0.997334 ns).

**Path 3 (truncated in the tool output).** Starts at `op[0]`, ends at flip-flop `_348_`, and shares Path 2's cells up to `_256_`. Slack is not shown in the data I received.

Netlist instance names (`_351_`, `_342_`, `_348_`) are not mapped to RTL register names in the data, so I cannot say which result bit or flag each flop is.

## Assessment
Timing has about 2.9 ns of setup margin at the slow corner before layout. No synthesis-strategy change is needed. The opcode decode (`op[0]` through or3b `_178_`) is the common head of the worst paths; if post-route margin shrinks, upsizing or restructuring that decode would be the first lever.

## Not covered by this task's data
- Equivalence (eqy) between RTL and netlist: no result given; not proven yet, and it is blocking per my role.
- Flop count / unreset flops (REQ-011, REQ-016).
- Worst 10 paths (only 2 complete).
assumptions: All numbers are taken verbatim from reports/synth_tool.json; this is pre-layout STA with an ideal clock and no layout parasitics.
Setup WNS/TNS per corner are taken as 0 because every reported worst slack is positive; TNS is not explicitly reported by the tool.
Only three nominal corners (nom_tt_025C_1v80, nom_ss_100C_1v60, nom_ff_n40C_1v95) were analysed; min/max RC corners are not in the data.
Interpretation of _178_ as an opcode-decode term is inferred from its connection to op[0] and its fanout; netlist instance names are not mapped to RTL names in the data.
The 4.0 ns input/output delays in constraints.sdc are DEFAULT (30% of period) values, unchanged in this task.
open_issues: REQ-016 flop count (must be exactly 12) cannot be confirmed: cell_classes in synth_tool.json is empty. Need a cell-class or flop count from the synthesis stat report.
Equivalence check (eqy) RTL vs netlist has no result in the inputs; not proven = blocking for sign-off of synthesis.
Worst-path report is truncated: only 2 complete paths (plus 1 partial, endpoint _348_, slack not shown) are available instead of the worst 10.

I/O delay conflict for human (G1) decision: spec open_questions says assume 0 ns external I/O delay, while constraints.sdc uses a DEFAULT 4.0 ns (30% of period). The current SDC is the more conservative choice; I did not change it.
Fast-corner hold margin is the smallest (0.1389 ns at nom_ff_n40C_1v95) with an ideal clock; re-check after CTS.
Mapping of flops _351_, _342_, _348_ to RTL registers (result bits vs flags) is not in the data.
